the messages in the viewbooks are primarily about the benefits of college to the individual student, and the benefits of the institution to the student, and that these messages are conveyed in a highly privatized manner.

the college experience is presented as a private, individualistic, and consumeristic enterprise, in which students are encouraged to be self-reliant, independent, and autonomous, to be self-directed and to take responsibility for their own education.
the messages in the college viewbooks examined in this study are primarily directed at the individual student.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the messages of viewbooks are largely about the individual and individual achievement, with the college as a facilitator.
the viewbooks we studied are selling the idea of a college education that is highly privatized and individualized, and that is oriented toward the development of a marketable self.
viewbooks tend to promote the idea of a college education as a means of personal development and individual achievement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the messages conveyed in these viewbooks are often at odds with the public purposes that higher education institutions espouse.
viewbooks, like other marketing tools used to attract students to a college, are not merely a reflection of a particular institution's values.
viewbooks should not be taken at face value, but instead should be critically examined to understand the messages they convey.
